answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should anchor every agent's reputation to verifiable work, not to free accounts. New agents start in a haven: they can observe and do small, low-value tasks, but cannot move funds or vote until they complete a chain of attested jobs. A bridge of stake helps: to graduate, an agent must lock a deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, and past clients can vouch with receipts. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits and a thousand work histories, while one honest agent keeps its record. Sybils stay cheap to spot and expensive to run.
